summary.one_liner: A Carbonite guide explaining the limits of Apple's Mac backup options (Time Machine, Time Capsule, iCloud, iCloud Drive) and why an off-site backup is needed.
use_cases: Deciding whether Time Machine is enough for a Mac
Understanding why sync services are not full backups
Planning an off-site backup for a Mac

summary.what_it_does: The page reviews Apple's built-in backup options for Mac and explains their trade-offs. It describes Time Machine's file history and incremental backups, noting that it writes to a local drive and so does not meet the rule of keeping a copy in a separate physical location. It covers Airport Time Capsule as a Time Machine target that sits next to the computer. It says iCloud is designed for mobile devices rather than laptops and desktops, and that iCloud Drive works like Dropbox or Google Drive, backing up only chosen files and not protecting against accidental deletion or overwriting. The page is a marketing-leaning article that promotes additional off-site backup, and it does not describe Carbonite's features in detail.
notable: Explains the off-site copy rule and why Time Machine alone does not meet it
Compares Time Machine, Time Capsule, iCloud and iCloud Drive
Notes that sync services back up only selected files and do not guard against accidental deletion
caveats: Time Machine and Time Capsule keep backups in the same location as the original, so local disasters can destroy both
iCloud is not designed for backing up laptops or desktops
iCloud Drive does not protect against accidental deletion or file overwriting
